messages:
maria_sre: Heads-up — prod-infer is piling Pending pods. Lots of small jobs (0.5 GPU request) and scheduler keeps saying '0.5gpu unavailable' even though nodes show free fractional capacity. Anyone else seeing stranded GPU slices?

alex_dev: I see a spike in Pending with Fit errors. Can you paste `kubectl describe` for one of the pods?

maria_sre: attaching snippet from a failed pod: 
```
Events:
  Type    Reason            Age    From               Message
  ----    ------            ----   ----               -------
  Normal  Scheduled         2m     default-scheduler  0/12 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient gpu, 6 node(s) had volume node affinity.
  Warning FailedScheduling  2m     kube-scheduler     0/12 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient gpu.
```

suhail_ops: infra metrics show recent CA scale-ups added 4 nodes with 1 GPU each but many pods request 0.5 GPU and the scheduler can't co-locate two 0.5 pods on a single GPU because kubelet reports allocatable as fractional but our device plugin isn't aggregating slices. CA backfilled capacity but left 0.5 slots stranded.

autoscaler-bot: [CA] scaleUp triggered: nodepool-gpu-small +4 (requested by prod-infer namespace) — reason: unschedulable pods. New nodes are ready at 1765554500.

jen_infra: This looks like two separate problems: (1) device plugin / runtime not advertising slice packing so scheduler thinks each 0.5 consumes a full GPU, (2) CA expander and node labelling caused small nodes to be created rather than right-sized nodes that could host multiple 0.5 slices.

alex_dev: Quick check — are pods using limits = requests for GPU? If limits > requests scheduler uses limits for fit. Also any `topologyAware` constraints?

maria_sre: Most pods just set `resources.requests.gpu: 0.5` and no limits. They were written assuming vGPU packing worked. We recently changed the device plugin version on some nodepools (rolling) — might be a mismatch.

suhail_ops: I ran `kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NAME,ALLOCATABLE.GPU,ALLOCATED.GPU` and on the new nodes allocatable shows `1`, but allocated shows `0.5` for one pod and `0` for rest — scheduler still treats the remaining 0.5 as unavailable because the device plugin reports per-device IDs and we don't support multi-attach packing in kube-scheduler.

jen_infra: Proposed immediate mitigations: (A) temporarily relax requests to 1 GPU for pending high-priority jobs (not ideal), (B) adjust CA to prefer larger instance types in nodepool-gpu-small so each node can actually host two 0.5 pods according to plugin, or (C) roll back device plugin to the older version that correctly exposes fractional vGPUs.

ops-oncall: Can we try option B first? Change autoscaler to pick `nodepool-gpu-medium` (2g) as expansion target. Patch CA config with `--node-group-auto-discovery` priorities? I can flip expander to `most-pods` for that pool for a short window.

autoscaler-bot: [CA] expander changed to most-pods for nodepool-gpu-small at 1765556000 (manual).

maria_sre: After expander change we got 2 x 2-GPU nodes instead of 4 x 1-GPU. Scheduler placed the pending pods immediately, Pending dropped from 120 -> 12 in 4 minutes.

alex_dev: Long-term we should: 1) standardize device plugin across nodepools, 2) add a scheduler plugin to aggregate fractional GPUs or move to integer-only requests, 3) add metric `orphaned_gpu_seconds` and a dashboard for fractional waste.

jen_infra: I'll open a short RFC for nodepool sizing and CA expansion policy tomorrow. Action items: jen to RFC, suhail to audit device plugin versions across regions, alex to add grafana panel for leftover GPU.

maria_sre: Thanks team — temporary fix worked. Leaving this thread open for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
